sessions.title: Automation and Data Harmonization
presenters: Vendors: Pearl Street, Nira, Grid Unity, and others
ISO users: MISO, PJM, ERCOT, and others
sessions.priority: HIGHEST — this is the session this project was built for
prep_checklist: This project is a data-harmonization tool, not a single-region study. Automation and Data Harmonization is its natural home in the series.

Lead with the milestone data-coverage finding: post-IA completion is computable in 8 of 9 regions. SPP records no IA date on any withdrawn project; BPA has 611 withdrawals with zero IA dates. That is a harmonization problem in the DATA, which is exactly this session's subject.
The provenance-tier system (measured / derived / simulated) is itself a harmonization proposal worth showing.

Pearl Street, Nira and Grid Unity are commercial interconnection-study platforms — this is a vendor-heavy room. An independent, open-source, reproducible benchmark is a different and complementary thing; position it that way, not as a competing product.
Have REPRODUCE.md ready — it runs on keyless public data, which is the credibility asset in a room full of proprietary tooling.

Cluster-family naming is a concrete harmonization example: MISO uses DPP, SPP uses DISIS, and the non-ISO West has no shared vocabulary at all (36 entities, families including CLUSTER/TRANSITION/SURPLUS/GI/RSC).
